classification.difficultyReason: Recognise the shaded segment as a sector minus a triangle, infer the radius from two distances, and construct a right triangle to obtain the exact central angle and chord length.

content.prompt: Find the exact area of the shaded region of the circle shown in the diagram.

spec.description: Circle with centre O, a vertical chord perpendicular to the horizontal radius, and the minor segment to the right shaded light blue. Curved arrows separately label the centre-to-chord and chord-to-circumference distances as 2 cm.
spec.mathematics: Radius 4 cm; perpendicular distance from centre to chord 2 cm; chord endpoints at central directions ±60 degrees. No inferred measurements are printed.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied distances, the centre, chord, radius, right-angle marker and requested shaded region remain visible in the question.

answer.worked:
The radius is $r=2+2=4\text{ cm}$. Let $\alpha$ be half the angle subtended by the chord at the centre. The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord and its subtended angle.
$$\begin{align*}\cos\alpha&=\frac{2}{4}\\\alpha&=\frac{\pi}{3}\\\theta&=2\alpha=\frac{2\pi}{3}\end{align*}$$
Half the chord has length $\sqrt{4^2-2^2}=2\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$, so the full chord has length $4\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{sector}}&=\frac12(4)^2\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)=\frac{16\pi}{3}\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{triangle}}&=\frac12(4\sqrt{3})(2)=4\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{shaded}}&=\frac{16\pi}{3}-4\sqrt{3}\\A_{\text{shaded}}&=\frac43(4\pi-3\sqrt{3})\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
